verdict: Item identified and openly readable. The probe 403 on 2026-10-20 was not repeated: the item JSON answered 200 on 2026-11-04. licence: LOC: free to use and reuse unless a Rights Advisory is present; none present in the item record; credit line "Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division"
resolution: Scale 1:2400 ("1" = 200 feet), 121 x 72 cm manuscript on tracing linen. LOC JP2 7186 x 13687 px (13,495,108 bytes), TIFF master 295,067,312 bytes, IIIF manifest https://www.loc.gov/item/99446453/manifest.json. By computation from pixel size and printed sheet size (scan margins unknown) about 0.21-0.24 m of ground per pixel.

feeds_terrain: terrain/elev1863: this is the readable-label source the error model asks for. Larger scale than the 1:12,000 reduction (LOC 99448794) so more printed contour values are legible, which is the stated limit on trusted coverage (ELEV-NOTES section 9 item 1: 48 anchors, 14.2 percent of the sheet). Covers only the south and southwest part, so it cannot fill the north, east or town. Next step for the integrator: download the 13.5 MB JP2, georeference to the FFD frame, read labels, rerun elev1863_s5/s7/s8 (documented in ELEV-NOTES section 8).

source: NPS Gettysburg park GIS 1863 layers (Curtis Musselman, GNMP cartographer)
verdict: Method documented by the author himself in the 2001 Spatial Odyssey paper (Wayback copy of the dead nps.gov URL): GIS documented conditions for 1993, 1927, 1895 and 1863; large-scale features (woods, fields, orchards, roads) and small-scale (fences, lanes, trees); Warren 1868-69 via the 1886 Corps of Engineers tracing scanned at 300 dpi by LOC (the NARA copy was 72 dpi); affine registration on nine control points (building corners, fence intersections) then rubbersheeting. Data are not public; no download found; licence unknown. Layers were shared with Knowles (xyht).
reliability_tier_pdf: None (PDF); by this pass an NPS primary description of a derived product (R3 data)
access: request-only; sending any request is an owner-only act
licence: Unknown (no statement found)
resolution: Registered at the scale of the 1:2400 tracing; positional accuracy of the 1863 layers not published. The same paper reports park existing-conditions maps with 1-foot contours at 1:600 (local engineering firm) and a spring 1996 Adams County orthophoto with 2-ft pixels.
date: Paper 2001 (snapshot 12 Feb 2005); layers built since 1996 when full-time GIS staff began
